This pattern is most consistent with a post-infectious peripheral neuropathy with possible cranial nerve involvement and respiratory muscle weakness—classically Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS). Central causes (stroke) are less likely given bilateral limb involvement and sensory symptoms. Myasthenia gravis is less likely because numbness/tingling is not typical. We still need one discriminating respiratory/autonomic detail to strengthen GBS vs other neuromuscular causes and to assess severity.
